A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RORem work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. Both have 18 pages; the appendices are identical in text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original object-removal experiments, human evaluations, training-round comparisons, and discriminator results in Tables 1–3, with additional visual results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including RORem's human-evaluated success rates of 76.2% and 70.2% at the two tested resolutions in Table 2.

M1.justification: Equation (4) revises the stated distillation loss: v1 applies fixed fθ at t+k and trainable fψ at t, whereas v3 applies fψ at t+k and fθ at t. This localized objective correction matches the unchanged Figure 5; it does not establish an implementation change or retraining.

E1.justification: Both retain RORD/Mulan initialization, OpenImages training and testing, and DIV2K/Flicker2K final fine-tuning. Object-removal evaluation covers the same scenes at 512×512 and 1024×1024, with unchanged appendix examples.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Lama, SDXL-INP, INST, PPT, IP2P, CLIPAway, and DesignEdit. The discriminator variants in Table 3 and comparator participation in the appendix comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain 500 cases per resolution, five human evaluators, the same preprocessing and mask dilation, evaluation metrics, and training settings. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The training-round comparisons in Table 1 and Appendix C, discriminator training-data analyses in Table 3, and failure cases in Appendix F are unchanged. No new ablation, robustness test, or case-study evidence appears.

E5.justification: Both report the human-study averages in the same way. Neither introduces repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 corrects CLIPAway's swapped DINO/CLIP entries: at 512×512, (22.91, 0.75) becomes (0.75, 22.91); at 1024×1024, (22.42, 0.75) becomes (0.75, 22.42). Other numerical results and qualitative examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (4)'s mathematical loss definition changes the teacher/student assignment, resolving its inconsistency with Figure 5. This changes which function receives each input rather than merely renaming notation. Other equations and Appendix B's metric definitions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: human-in-the-loop data construction exceeding 200K pairs, robust SDXL-based object removal, four-step distillation, and the claimed roughly 18% success-rate advantage.

C2.justification: The conclusion retains the VAE-detail and finger/small-face limitations, but now emphasizes that the latter persist despite task-specific adaptation. It adds SD3 or Flux as possible future remedies; the supporting failure examples remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, including LoRA ranks, optimization settings, training steps, hardware, annotation interfaces, and preprocessing instructions, are unchanged. Both retain the same dataset, code, and model access statement and repository link.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 72 references are unchanged after accounting for bibliography reflow. The future-work mention of SD3/Flux does not revise the paper's novelty or research positioning.

P1.justification: A short rewrite and extension of the concluding limitations paragraph adds explanatory wording and future work. Section order, the remaining narrative, and appendix text are unchanged, apart from version/date text.

P2.justification: The longer conclusion continues into the right column and shifts the bibliography across columns and pages 9–12. Figures, table structures, captions, and appendix layouts remain unchanged; Table 2's numerical corrections do not constitute a table redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the distillation formula to match the existing diagram and fixes misplaced CLIPAway metrics, improving mathematical and reporting consistency. The more specific future-work discussion adds limited clarification. These are useful, localized improvements, with the empirical evidence and main conclusions retained.
